title: (No AI) Nothing teases a screen-free AI device ahead of launch next month
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![Photo of camera of Nothing Phone 4A in front of plants.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/03/nothing-phone-4a-2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Nothing CEO Carl Pei said in [a post on X](https://x.com/getpeid/status/2117991714879410204) that the company's launching its first AI device in December. That's just a little over a year after Pei announced [plans for "AI-native" devices](https://www.theverge.com/news/778636/nothing-ai-native-devices) and an AI operating system. He didn't give away much about what exactly the new device is, only that one feature it _won't_ have is a screen:

> "Our first AI-native product ships next month. It's a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn't have been an app."

Pei shared an image with the post that says "NOTHING(R)" in the top left corner, above an ambiguous black rounded …

author: Victoria Song
content:

Also, can I just say this LED indicator light is way too small and unnoticeable?

_This is_ [Optimizer](https://www.theverge.com/optimizer-newsletter)_, a weekly newsletter sent from_ Verge _senior reviewer_ [_Victoria Song_](https://www.theverge.com/authors/victoria-song) _that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for_ Optimizer _[here](https://www.theverge.com/newsletters)._

"How does that make you feel?"

I get asked this a lot in therapy. Plenty of life events, big and small, have triggered this question.
